questions.q: What is the key security difference between a Basic and a Standard Azure Public IP?
options: Standard is secure by default and denies inbound traffic unless an NSG explicitly allows it; Basic was open by default
Basic is more secure because it has no public internet exposure at all
There is no security difference — only the SLA differs between the two SKUs
Standard SKU cannot be used with any NSG, while Basic requires one
questions.explain: Standard SKU public IPs deny all inbound traffic unless an NSG explicitly allows it, while Basic SKU was open by default and relied entirely on NSGs for restriction.

questions.q: At which OSI layer does Azure Load Balancer operate?
options: Layer 4 — it distributes TCP/UDP traffic by IP address and port without inspecting application content
Layer 7 — it inspects HTTP headers and URL paths to make routing decisions
Layer 2 — it operates purely on MAC addresses
Layer 3 only, and does not consider port numbers at all
questions.explain: Azure Load Balancer is a Layer 4 device: it routes TCP and UDP traffic based on IP address and port only, unlike Layer 7 services such as Application Gateway.

questions.q: What three components must be configured together for an Azure Load Balancer to distribute traffic correctly?
options: A backend pool, a health probe, and a load balancing rule
A VNet, a subnet, and a route table
A public IP, a resource group, and a region
An NSG, a VNet peering, and a DNS zone
questions.explain: A backend pool defines the targets, a health probe checks their status, and a load balancing rule maps a frontend IP:port to the backend pool using the probe's results.

questions.q: What happens to a backend instance that fails enough consecutive health probe checks?
options: It is automatically pulled out of rotation and receives no new traffic until it passes the probe again
The load balancer rule is deleted entirely
Azure automatically restarts the VM
Nothing — health probes only generate log entries and don't affect traffic routing
questions.explain: An unhealthy backend instance is automatically removed from active rotation; the load balancer resumes sending it traffic once it passes the health probe again.

questions.q: A Standard SKU load balancer's backend pool, probe, and rule are all configured correctly, but no traffic is reaching the backend VMs. What's the most likely cause?
options: Missing NSG rule allowing the expected traffic — Standard SKU denies inbound traffic by default
The load balancer must be recreated using the Basic SKU instead
Health probes are not supported on Standard SKU load balancers
Standard SKU load balancers require a VPN gateway to function at all
questions.explain: Because Standard SKU is secure by default, a missing NSG allow rule is the most common reason traffic (including probe traffic) is silently dropped despite correct load balancer configuration.
